source_text: Μηδὲ λῦε τὸν τῆς ψυχῆς τόνον ἐν εὐωχίᾳ καὶ ποτῶν ἀνέσει, ἱκανὸν δὲ ἡγοῦ τῷ σώματι τὸ χρειῶδες. καὶ μὴ πρόσθεν ἐπείγου πρὸς τροφὰς πρὶν ἢ καὶ δείπνου παρῇ καιρός· ἄρτος δὲ ἔστω σοι τὸ δεῖπνον, καὶ πόαι γῆς προσέστωσαν καὶ τὰ ἐκ δένδρων ὡραῖα· ἴθι δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν τροφὴν εὐσταθῶς καὶ μὴ λυσσώδη γαστριμαργίαν ἐπιφαίνων· μηδὲ σαρκοβόρος μηδὲ φίλοινος ἔσο, ὁπότε μὴ νόσος τις ἴασιν ἐπὶ ταύτην ἄγοι. ἀλλ’ ἀντὶ τῶν ἐν τούτοις ἡδονῶν τὰς ἐν λόγοις θείοις καὶ ὕμνοις εὐφροσύνας αἱροῦ τῇ παρὰ θεοῦ σοι χορηγουμένας σοφίᾳ, οὐράνιός τε ἀεί σε φροντὶς ἀναγέτω πρὸς οὐρανόν.
orientation: Clement continues his direct moral instruction to the newly baptized, now turning from prayer and joy in Christ to rules for food, drink, and keeping the soul's firmness.
pass_a_gloss: Do not loosen the firmness of the soul in feasting and in relaxation of drinks, but consider sufficient for the body what is needful. And do not hurry beforehand to foods before the time of dinner is also present; but let bread be your dinner, and let herbs of the earth be present and the ripe fruits from trees; and go to the food steadily and not displaying rabid gluttony; and do not be a meat-eater nor a wine-lover, whenever some illness does not lead to this for healing. But instead of the pleasures in these things choose the joys in divine words and hymns, the joys supplied to you by the wisdom from God, and let heavenly thought always lead you up to heaven.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'firmness of soul' for τόνος τῆς ψυχῆς, and the verb λῦε means to loosen or dissolve, so the image is of slackening the soul's tension.
ἄνεσις means loosening or relaxation; paired with feasting it suggests the slackening effect of drinking, not just the drinks themselves.
λυσσώδης means rabid or frenzied, and the glossary gives 'gluttony' for γαστριμαργία; the adjective intensifies the passion as a mad, uncontrolled appetite.
The compound means flesh-eating; rendering it as a noun preserves the categorical prohibition and the literal sense.
The compound means wine-loving; a literal noun rendering keeps the parallel with meat-eater and the categorical force.

choices.term: οὐράνιός τε ἀεί σε φροντὶς ἀναγέτω πρὸς οὐρανόν
choices.english: and let heavenly thought always lead you up to heaven
choices.why: φροντίς is thought or care; 'heavenly thought' preserves the adjective-noun structure and the upward motion of ἀναγέτω.

pass_b_english: Do not loosen the firmness of your soul in feasting and the relaxation of drinks; consider what is necessary sufficient for the body. Do not hurry to food before the time for dinner has come. Let bread be your dinner, with herbs of the earth and ripe fruits from the trees. Go to your food calmly, not displaying rabid gluttony. Do not be a meat-eater or a wine-lover, unless some illness leads you to these things for healing. Instead of the pleasures found in them, choose the joys of divine words and hymns, given to you by the wisdom that comes from God, and let heavenly thought always lead you up to heaven.

last_rejected.why: λυσσώδη means sloppy or loose, not violent; "rabid" adds intensity not in the Greek.
last_rejected.ruling: λυσσώδη derives from λύσσα (rabies/madness); 'rabid gluttony' is standard and accurate.

problems.why: 'Rabid' is bizarrely modern/medical for ancient context; suggests hydrophobia, not eagerness.

fixed: Changed 'rabid gluttony' to 'ravenous gluttony': λυσσώδη means 'raging, frenzied' in the sense of mad eagerness, not the modern medical sense of rabies; 'ravenous' fits the context of gluttony better.
